Subject: Renewal + surge capacity — pricing questions

Hi Mateo,

We're kicking off renewal planning for our account (term ends 2026-12-31) and want to lock in a clear path for an expected Q4 surge. A few things we want to confirm from Redwood before we loop procurement:

- Pricing for a temporary 2x capacity spike for 3 months (Oct-Dec) — is there an uplift rate vs. committed units?
- Can we co-term the expanded capacity to the existing 12/31 renewal date (i.e., amend vs. new 12-month top-up)?
- Any pro-rata/invoice timing constraints — we need this to align with our budget cycle and PO cut-off (first week of Aug).

If you can send initial uplift scenarios and estimated invoice timing by next week, I'll share with procurement and legal.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
Head of AI Product
Novacorp

P.S. Procurement asked whether you can attach an example amendment and a sample PO template to help speed review.

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + surge capacity — pricing questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask, appreciate the timelines. High-level options below (we can formalize once you confirm which path you prefer):

1) Staged uplift (recommended for predictability)
   - Add a 3-month surge bucket Oct-Dec sized at 2x your current committed units.
   - Pricing: uplift multiplier of 1.10x the committed unit rate for the first 2x, 1.20x thereafter (if usage exceeds the surge bucket).
   - Co-term: we can amend the contract so the surge is billed pro-rata and co-terms to your 12/31 renewal.

2) Top-up with single invoice (simpler, less paperwork)
   - One-off top-up purchase at 1.08x rate for the exact additional units; invoice up-front for the quarter.

3) Flat monthly add-on (smoother cash flow)
   - Convert expected surge into a temporary monthly seat/throughput add-on; 10% discount if you commit to an estimate window by Aug 3.

Administrative notes:
- We can provide a draft amendment and sample PO (I'll attach both).
- Legal turnaround: typical 5–7 business days for a standard amendment; expedited review possible with an annotated change list.
- To meet your PO timeline, we need a short confirmation (preferred option) by Aug 3.

I'll loop in Kimberly for the exact numbers and a simple workbook that lays out invoice scenarios.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com

Hi Elena / team — attaching a short workbook that models three priced scenarios and an amendment draft (both attached). Summary here so it's easier to share with procurement: 

Scenario A — Surge bucket (recommended for flexibility)- Size: 2x committed units for Oct-Dec- Pricing: 10% uplift on unit rate for bucket (applied to allowed surge), 20% uplift above bucket- Billing: prorated by month, single invoice for the surge period after month-end

Scenario B — Prepaid top-up- Size: exact additional capacity purchased up-front- Pricing: 8% uplift vs committed unit rate- Billing: invoice issued on execution, non-refundable (best for predictable cashflow)

Scenario C — Monthly add-on (smoothing)- Size: expected monthly surge converted to temporary add-on- Pricing: 10% discount if Novacorp signs commit estimate by Aug 3- Billing: monthly invoicing with adjustment if overs/unders occur

Notes on co-term: all three paths can be implemented as an amendment that co-terms to 12/31. If you prefer the prepaid top-up we mirror the pro-rata treatment to align with your fiscal needs.

I've attached: uplift-pricing-model.xlsx, co-term-amend-draft.docx, novacorp-po-template.pdf.

Next steps suggestion: Elena confirms preferred scenario and whether procurement needs expedited legal redlines. If yes, we can prioritize and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Pricing & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

1) Pricing hold: we can hold the Scenario A uplift pricing through Aug 15 for execution without requiring a signed PO prior to that date.
2) Invoice cadence: we'll issue monthly invoices at month-end for Oct/Nov/Dec (post-month). We can also provide a consolidated summary invoice after Dec if your procurement team prefers a single reconciliation.
3) Legal & DocuSign: we'll prepare an amendment and aim for an expedited 3 business-day review on our side if you supply a short annotated redline. We'll generate a DocuSign envelope and share the link by end of week.
4) PO timeline: to guarantee capacity, we'd ask for a formal PO signed by Aug 3 ideally, but the pricing hold until Aug 15 provides a small buffer.
